What you can get

Finding one

About 1 in 2,500 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

What it paints

Each outcome, described the way the gene file describes it, and then the layers that draw it in the order they are painted. The prose is the part a reader checks a bake against; the list underneath is what the engine actually did.

Valentine Appaloosa

Two things at once. First the base shifts: wherever the coat was black it comes out saturated red or fuchsia, and wherever it was red it comes out pink, mane and tail included - so there is no such thing as a dull Valentine. Then the appaloosa half puts white spots over it, in any of the usual arrangements: a blanket over the hindquarter, leopard spotting over the whole horse, a fine snowflake scatter, or a varnish roan. Some horses show the reverse as well, with white cut-outs left in the colour rather than laid on it.

  1. black pigment to fuchsia — PIGMENT, painted with TOWARD
  2. red pigment to pink — PIGMENT × PIGMENT inverted, painted with TOWARD
  3. the white blanket over the hindquarter — PATCHES × AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  4. spots over the blanket and beyond it — SPOTS, painted with TOWARD
